claim.spatial_precision: cotton-harvest labour system and monitored recruitment; country entity is index/context, not a prevalence polygon
claim.summary: ILO third-party monitoring of Uzbekistan's 2019 cotton harvest found that systematic central recruitment had ended but recorded remaining forced labour and involuntary recruitment, especially at local level. The atlas therefore records a positive forced-labour claim for the 2019 cotton-harvest system while preserving the documented improvement and refusing to convert monitored counts into a national prevalence estimate.
claim.notes: Reconciles legacy claim 3b8c4fa4-8765-488c-a814-399169638bf3 into current post-M1 semantics. No new P-level is assigned. Legacy geometry 053f546e-089e-4f03-aab7-3d2187c835ce is an explicit modern/navigation proxy and is not promoted as this claim's historical/practice inference extent.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive bounded classification only. Do not infer national prevalence, uniform territorial distribution, legal status, or a country-wide practice polygon beyond what the evidence directly supports.

source.title: 2019 Third-party monitoring of child labour and forced labour during the cotton harvest in Uzbekistan
source.independence_notes: ILO third-party monitoring programme. Monitoring counts and the narrative finding belong to one evidence family.
source.reliability_limitations: Observed forced-labour counts are monitoring results, not a country-wide prevalence rate. The report also records major reduction and the end of systematic central recruitment.
